title: Which role card needs work?
scenario: A studio drafts role cards for a four-role team that will make localised ads. You check the cards before the team starts. The cards are our own examples, made up for this case. Use the exhibit.
exhibit:
ROLE CARDS (draft, made up for this case):
  Producer      Job: plan the run, hand out items, collect results.
                Tools: the status sheet.
  Localiser     Job: "Translate the ad."
                Tools: all tools.
  Visual maker  Job: make one image from the approved line and the layout file.
                Output: one PNG named with the item id.
                Tools: the image tool.
  Copy checker  Job: check each tagline for length (40 characters or fewer)
                and for banned words.
                Output: pass or fail, with the reason.
                Tools: read text files.

questions.prompt: Which role card is weakest, and why?

options.text: Producer, because it has no tool that makes assets and so it cannot get anything done
options.explanation: The producer plans and collects. It should not make assets, so that is not a flaw.

options.text: Localiser, because its job is vague and it holds every tool, so it has no clear limits
options.explanation: Right. Anthropic says helpers need an objective, an output format, guidance on tools and clear boundaries. This card has only a vague objective and none of the other three.

options.text: Visual maker, because it names one output file, and a role should not name its output
options.explanation: A named output is what a good card has. It tells the next role what to expect.

options.text: Copy checker, because its job is only pass or fail, and a role needs a longer description
options.explanation: A short, narrow job is a strength. OpenAI says to give each specialist a narrow job.

questions.prompt: Ten Localiser helpers all get the card as written. What is the most likely result?

options.text: Every helper writes the same line, because they all read one card and reach one answer
options.explanation: They have no market to work on, so they would not all give the same line. The problem is duplicates and gaps.

options.text: The helpers ask the producer which market to use, because a model asks first
options.explanation: Nothing makes a model ask. Do not plan on it.

options.text: Some helpers repeat a market and some are skipped, because nothing says which is theirs
options.explanation: Right. Anthropic reports that vague instructions led agents to duplicate work and leave gaps.

options.text: Each helper takes a different market in turn, because models share out work fairly alone
options.explanation: Anthropic found the opposite with short instructions: helpers repeated each other.

questions.prompt: Which tool list fits the Localiser best?

options.text: None, because it only returns one line of text and needs no tool at all for this job
options.explanation: Right. Claude lists tool restrictions as a benefit of subagents. A role should hold only what its job needs.

options.text: Web search and the image tool, so that it can test how the line looks in a picture
options.explanation: Making the picture is the Visual maker's job. Extra tools add risk and no value here.

options.text: The posting tool only, so that finished lines can go live as soon as they are written
options.explanation: Nothing is approved yet. Posting belongs to a later step with a person's sign-off.

options.text: All tools, so that it never has to wait for another role to help it finish a line
options.explanation: Claude says to limit subagents to specific tools to reduce the risk of unintended actions.

questions.prompt: Which role is the best one to try on a smaller, cheaper model first?

options.text: The Producer, because planning is simple and any model can hand out ten items
options.explanation: The producer decides what to do when a step fails. That is judgment, so it is a poor first test.

options.text: The Localiser, because language work is easy and needs no strong model
options.explanation: Tone and meaning in another language are not always easy. Do not assume it.

options.text: The Visual maker, because the picture comes from a tool and the model only passes text
options.explanation: The model writes the prompt that decides the picture. Quality can drop.

options.text: The Copy checker, because counting characters and matching a word list is plain work
options.explanation: Right. Anthropic's routing example sends easy, common work to smaller, cost-efficient models. Claude subagents can also use their own model. Test it first.
